title: Remarks at Richardton, North Dakota
paragraphs: I am awfully glad to see you my old neighbors and friends. As I have come through North Dakota to-day the farther west I have gotten the more I felt just exactly as if I was getting back to my home. There is hardly a town we have come to where there are not some friends with whom I worked in the past days, atwhose houses I slept in the old times. Twenty-three years ago I came to Dakota. It was a territory then. It was twenty years ago that I first worked around here.
I recollect in the old days I used to ship cattle from Dickinson, and half of the time that I would go by here it would be on a cattle train.
I wish you well, and am very glad to have had the chance of greeting you. (Cheers and applause)
